summary: Round-2 fixes are sound on their own merits: campaigns.service.ts's dtoToEntity correctly threads current.metadata into update() (verified with a genuine spec test that would fail if the merge were reverted) and passes no currentMetadata on create() (default {} is correct, nothing to preserve). lead-events.handler.ts's onLeadConverted now wraps the read-check-write sequence in base.transaction() with pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(...)) as the first statement inside the callback -- verified against TypeORM's actual EntityManager.transaction()/PostgresQueryRunner.startTransaction() source: when manager is already an open transaction (session-context ON) TypeORM issues a real SAVEPOINT (not a silent no-op), and each of the three write steps in convertLead still has its own try/catch that logs and swallows, so no unexpected error can now escape and abort an outer transaction that previously wouldn't have aborted, nor does the restructuring hide a failure that should abort. Lock key lead-conversion:tenantId:leadId is parameterized (no injection) and UUID components make key collisions across different leads via string concatenation practically impossible; hashtext 32-bit collisions are a benign extra-contention risk, not a correctness bug. HOWEVER: running the exact shared spec file the task asked me to check (event-handlers-context-propagation.spec.ts) produces 1 FAILING test unrelated to the two fixes under review -- ArtistWorkflowHandler creates onboarding tasks inside tenant context fails because artist-workflow.handler.ts now gates on ArtistStatus.SIGNED (signed) while contract-events.handler.ts still writes the legacy literal contratado to the artist status column, so onboarding-task creation silently no-ops for that path (find-82d0f73a). This is a real, reproducible regression in the current workspace and the shared test file is currently red, so Wave 8 regression review cannot close PASS as-is.
